cards.title: When Motherhood Reactivates Unresolved Trauma
cards.body: Becoming a mother can awaken unresolved trauma, bringing old relational patterns and triggers into the present. Understanding how past wounds resurface during motherhood helps parents address these challenges.

cards.title: What Can I Do When My Child Rejects Me?
cards.body: Divorce can rupture family relationships and trust, leaving parents struggling with rejection. Healing can begin even when reconciliation hasn't started, offering hope for reconnection.

cards.title: Back to School Teen Social Scene
cards.body: New school years require social adjustment, and teens have different social wiring. Parents can help by understanding their teen's unique needs and supporting their social development.

cards.title: Play Is Serious Business: Let Kids Have Fun!
cards.body: As recess has declined from three times daily to none, academic achievement has fallen and obesity risen. Prioritizing play and fun is essential for children's development and wellbeing.

cards.title: 7 Ways Emotional Neglect Differs in Men and Women
cards.body: Childhood emotional neglect leaves the same core wound in everyone but surfaces differently in men and women. Recognizing these differences helps parents understand and prevent patterns of neglect.

cards.title: Music Festivals Aren't Worse With Children
cards.body: Parents can bring toddlers to music festivals without spoiling the experience—families add magic to events. Taking kids to festivals teaches them to embrace joy and adventure.

cards.title: Maternity Care Access and Family Safety
cards.body: Expecting mothers deserve access to safe maternity care without financial barriers. Universal state care is essential so all families feel supported during birth.

cards.title: Financial Favoritism Between Adult Children
cards.body: When parents lend money to one child but not another, it can cause lasting jealousy and resentment. Experts suggest transparent conversations to prevent long-term family damage.

cards.title: I've Got Feelings for My Child's Teacher
cards.body: Crushes feel freeing because they operate outside everyday life, but acting on them risks your family's stability. Therapists suggest examining whether these feelings reflect unmet needs in your marriage.
